activities.title: Descriptive statistics: mean, spread, and honest summaries

source_resources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods
source_resources.author: NIST (U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology) and SEMATECH
source_resources.license: NIST public information (U.S. government site; NIST/SEMATECH co-production)
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external linking to NIST public information, which NIST policy allows to be distributed or copied unless marked copyrighted; no source text is imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: High-school arithmetic; no calculus required for the descriptive sections.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary engineering reference for descriptive statistics, exploratory data analysis, and uncertainty quantification with worked formulas.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Hosted on itl.nist.gov; a U.S. government site generally accessible worldwide.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Every formula used in the lesson (mean, variance, standard error) is reproduced as original explanation; all exercises run fully offline.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Undergraduate statistics text with a stronger narrative bridge from probability to inference; retained as the second linked source for inferential framing.
Strong interactive visualizations of probability and sampling, but a browser-only interactive format is a weaker fit for an offline-capable 480-minute ledger.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 1.3.5 (Quantitative Techniques): measures of location and scale

source_resources.title: OpenIntro Statistics (4th edition)
source_resources.author: David Diez, Mine Cetinkaya-Rundel, Christopher Barr
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external linking under CC BY-SA 3.0; the share-alike condition applies to derivative text and no source text is imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Introductory algebra; comfort reading mathematical notation.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Rigorous open textbook treatment of sampling distributions, standard error, and the difference between an inferential claim and an anecdotal observation.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Free PDF and web distribution via openintro.org; print editions are commercial.
source_resources.safe_fallback: All required definitions and worked computations are given in the lesson itself; the book is a further-reading link.

compared_candidates.license: NIST public information (U.S. government site; NIST/SEMATECH co-production)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Engineering handbook strength for formulas, tables, and measurement practice; OpenIntro supplies the probability-to-inference narrative.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Stat 110: Introduction to Probability (Harvard, Prof. Joe Blitzstein)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Strong probability course, but lectures and the print book are under full copyright and the syllabus spans a semester rather than a single study block.
